newsitem.title: USA: Rain from Hurricane aids North Carolina crops.
newsitem.headline: Rain from Hurricane aids North Carolina crops.

text.p: The remanents of Hurricane Danny damaged some North Carolina crops during the week ended Sunday, but most crops will benefit from the much-needed moisture, said the state's Agricultural Statistics Service's weekly report.
Most areas that were starting to report drought damage did get rain, the report said.

Corn was 22 percent dented, 63 was in the dough stage, and 91 had silked versus 32, 79 and 97, respectively, a year ago and the 41, 71, and 95 averages. The crop was rated one percent excellent, 38 good, 39 fair, 17 poor and five very poor.
Twenty eight percent of the soybeans were blooming versus 32 a year ago and the 28 average. The crop was rated four percent excellent, 63 good, 28 fair, four poor and one very poor.

Sixty percent of the cotton was setting bolls and 86 had squared versus 75 and 95, respectively, a year ago and the 65 and 88 averages. The crop was rated five percent excellent, 48 good, 38 fair, six poor and three poor.
Soil moisture was rated 17 percent surplus, 59 adequate, 19 short and five very short.
